title: 1 Kings Chapter 12 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Kings chapter 12 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Kings Chapter 12 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Kings Chapter 12.

questions.question: Where did Rehoboam go to be made king?
questions.correctAnswer: Shechem
questions.explanation: Rehoboam went to Shechem because all Israel had come there to make him king, as stated in 1 Kings 12:1.

questions.question: Where was Jeroboam when he heard that Rehoboam was going to be made king?
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt
questions.explanation: Jeroboam was in Egypt, having fled from King Solomon's presence, as stated in 1 Kings 12:2.

questions.question: Who came and spoke to Rehoboam asking him to lighten the heavy yoke of his father?
options: Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel
questions.explanation: Jeroboam and all the congregation of Israel came and spoke to Rehoboam requesting lighter burdens, as recorded in 1 Kings 12:3.

questions.question: What did the people ask Rehoboam to do about the heavy yoke?
questions.correctAnswer: Make the grievous service lighter
questions.explanation: They asked Rehoboam to make the grievous service and heavy yoke lighter as his father had made it grievous, as per 1 Kings 12:4.

questions.question: How many days did Rehoboam ask the people to depart before he would answer them?
questions.correctAnswer: Three days
questions.explanation: Rehoboam told the people to depart for three days and then come back for his answer, according to 1 Kings 12:5.

questions.question: Whom did Rehoboam first consult for advice on how to answer the people?
options: The old men who stood before Solomon
The young men who grew up with him
questions.correctAnswer: The old men who stood before Solomon
questions.explanation: Rehoboam first consulted the old men who served Solomon for advice, as stated in 1 Kings 12:6.

questions.question: What advice did the old men give to Rehoboam?
options: Serve the people and speak good words to them
Increase the burdens on the people
questions.correctAnswer: Serve the people and speak good words to them
questions.explanation: The old men advised Rehoboam to serve the people and speak good words so they would serve him forever, found in 1 Kings 12:7.

questions.question: Who did Rehoboam consult after he forsook the counsel of the old men?
options: The young men who grew up with him
questions.correctAnswer: The young men who grew up with him
questions.explanation: Rehoboam consulted the young men who were grown up with him after forsaking the old men's counsel, as explained in 1 Kings 12:8.

questions.question: What did the young men advise Rehoboam to say to the people?
options: My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins
Let us negotiate a new yoke
questions.correctAnswer: My little finger shall be thicker than my father's loins
questions.explanation: The young men advised Rehoboam to say that his little finger would be thicker than his father's loins, indicating he would be harsher, as given in 1 Kings 12:10.

questions.question: According to the young men, how would Rehoboam chastise the people compared to his father?
questions.correctAnswer: With scorpions instead of whips
questions.explanation: The young men said Rehoboam would chastise the people with scorpions, adding to the heavy yoke and harsher than his father's whips, as described in 1 Kings 12:11.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam accepted the advice of the old men and spoke kindly to the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Rehoboam rejected the old men's counsel and spoke roughly to the people, following the young men's advice (1 Kings 12:13-14).

questions.question: True or False: The people of Israel said they had no inheritance in the son of Jesse.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The people said, 'What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse,' as recorded in 1 Kings 12:16.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam reigned over all Israel after the people rejected him.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Rehoboam only reigned over the children of Judah who dwelt in the cities of Judah; the rest of Israel departed, as shown in 1 Kings 12:17.

questions.question: True or False: Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, but he was stoned to death by Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: King Rehoboam sent Adoram over the tribute, but Israel stoned him to death, as stated in 1 Kings 12:18.

questions.question: In 1 Kings 12, which event happened first?
options: Rehoboam sent Adoram over the tribute
Jeroboam was made king over all Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam consulted the old men
questions.explanation: Rehoboam consulting the old men happened early when deciding how to respond to the people's request, as shown in 1 Kings 12:6, which occurs before the other events.

medium.title: 1 Kings Chapter 12 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Kings Chapter 12 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How did King Rehoboam respond to the people's request to lighten the heavy yoke his father put on them?
options: He promised to make their yoke lighter
He ignored them and made no reply
He threatened to increase their burden and chastise them more harshly
He consulted the old men again and followed their advice
questions.correctAnswer: He threatened to increase their burden and chastise them more harshly
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 12:14, Rehoboam spoke to the people after the counsel of the young men, saying he would add to their yoke and chastise them with scorpions, increasing their burden rather than lightening it. This was after he forsook the old men's counsel (verses 13-14).

questions.question: What was the primary reason given for Rehoboam's refusal to heed the people's request, according to the chapter?
options: He wanted to show strength to his enemies
He was pressured by his advisors to be harsh
It was the LORD's purpose to fulfill His word through Ahijah the Shilonite
He feared losing his throne if he yielded
questions.correctAnswer: It was the LORD's purpose to fulfill His word through Ahijah the Shilonite
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:15 explains that the king's refusal to listen was from the LORD, so that He might fulfill His prophecy spoken by Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam. This shows God's sovereign plan was behind the division.

questions.question: What was the reaction of all Israel when they saw that King Rehoboam would not lighten their yoke?
options: They declared loyalty to the house of David
They rejected David's dynasty and returned to their tents
They requested another meeting to negotiate
questions.correctAnswer: They rejected David's dynasty and returned to their tents
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:16 records that Israel said to the king, 'What portion have we in David?' and returned to their tents, signifying their rejection of Rehoboam and the house of David after he refused their request.

questions.question: Which tribes remained loyal to Rehoboam after Israel's rebellion?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah and Benjamin
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:17 and 12:21 show that Rehoboam reigned over the children of Israel dwelling in Judah's cities and that he assembled the house of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin to fight against Israel, indicating their loyalty to him.

questions.question: What happened to Adoram, the officer over tribute, when sent by King Rehoboam?
options: He was stoned to death by all Israel
questions.correctAnswer: He was stoned to death by all Israel
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 12:18, when Rehoboam sent Adoram, who was over the tribute, all Israel stoned him with stones, leading to his death, showing the people's violent rejection of Rehoboam's authority.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 12 teach about the importance of heeding wise counsel?
options: It shows that ignoring wise counsel can lead to division and rebellion
It encourages leaders to always choose the advice of younger advisors
It states that counsel is unnecessary when one is king
It suggests that harshness is the best way to maintain control
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that ignoring wise counsel can lead to division and rebellion
questions.explanation: Rehoboam ignored the old men's counsel who advised gentleness (verses 6-7) and instead followed the young men's harsh advice (verses 8-14), resulting in the kingdom splitting and rebellion (verses 16-19), illustrating the consequences of rejecting wisdom.

questions.question: What did the LORD command through Shemaiah to Rehoboam and his assembled army?
options: To attack Israel and reclaim the kingdom
To retreat and not fight their brethren
To seek an alliance with Egypt
To build stronger fortifications in Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: To retreat and not fight their brethren
questions.explanation: In 1 Kings 12:22-24, God spoke to Shemaiah, commanding Rehoboam and the people of Judah and Benjamin not to fight their brethren Israel and to return to their homes, indicating divine intervention to prevent civil war.

questions.question: True or False: After the kingdom split, all the tribes of Israel rejected Jeroboam's kingship.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:20 states that all Israel sent and called Jeroboam and made him king over all Israel, except the tribe of Judah, which alone followed the house of David, so the statement is false.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 12:24 promise will happen if Rehoboam and his army obey God's word through Shemaiah?
options: They will be victorious in battle
They will receive peace by returning to their homes
They will conquer Israel and reunify the kingdom
They will gain wealth from their enemies
questions.correctAnswer: They will receive peace by returning to their homes
questions.explanation: Verse 24 says they hearkened to the word of the LORD and returned to depart, implying that obedience leads to peace rather than conflict among brethren, fulfilling God's will.

questions.question: How did the people of Israel's attitude toward the house of David change after Rehoboam's harsh response?
options: They declared they had no inheritance in David's son
They requested a new king from David's lineage
questions.correctAnswer: They declared they had no inheritance in David's son
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:16 records the people saying, 'What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse,' indicating a complete rejection of Rehoboam and David's family after his harsh reply.

questions.question: What lesson about leadership can be drawn from Rehoboam assembling 180,000 chosen warriors?
options: Leadership requires seeking God's will before action
Strength is the ultimate solution to conflict
questions.correctAnswer: Leadership requires seeking God's will before action
questions.explanation: Though Rehoboam assembled a large army (verse 21), God commanded through Shemaiah not to fight (verses 22-24), teaching that leaders should seek and obey God's guidance rather than rely solely on military strength.

questions.question: True or False: The rebellion of Israel against the house of David was a temporary event that ended quickly.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:19 states, 'So Israel rebelled against the house of David unto this day,' indicating the rebellion was ongoing and persistent, so the statement is false.

questions.question: What does 1 Kings 12 teach about the consequences of prideful leadership ignoring the people's needs?
options: It causes division and loss of loyalty
questions.correctAnswer: It causes division and loss of loyalty
questions.explanation: Rehoboam's prideful refusal to lighten the people's burden caused all Israel except Judah to rebel and reject his rule (verses 13-16), showing that prideful leadership can fracture unity and loyalty.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam returned from Egypt and was immediately accepted by all Israel as their king.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:20 states that all Israel sent and called Jeroboam, making him king over all Israel except Judah, confirming that he was accepted upon his return.

questions.question: What practical Christian virtue is demonstrated by the people hearkening to God's word and returning to their homes instead of fighting?
questions.correctAnswer: Faith and obedience
questions.explanation: In verses 22-24, the people obey God's word through Shemaiah by refraining from fighting their brethren and returning home, demonstrating faith in God's command and obedience to His will.

hard.title: 1 Kings Chapter 12 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Kings Chapter 12.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give to Rehoboam and the house of Judah and Benjamin through Shemaiah?
options: To fight against the house of Israel
To return every man to his house and not fight
To build new cities for defense
questions.correctAnswer: To return every man to his house and not fight
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:24 states that the LORD commanded them not to fight but to return to their homes, for this division was from Him.

questions.question: Which cities did Jeroboam build and dwell in after the division of the kingdom?
questions.correctAnswer: Shechem and Penuel
questions.explanation: According to 1 Kings 12:25, Jeroboam built Shechem in mount Ephraim, dwelt there, and later built Penuel.

questions.question: Why did Jeroboam create two golden calves and set them in Bethel and Dan?
options: To honor the LORD in multiple locations
To prevent the people from going to Jerusalem to worship
To symbolize the unity of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: To prevent the people from going to Jerusalem to worship
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:28-29 explains Jeroboam's fear that the people's hearts would return to Rehoboam if they went to Jerusalem, so he made golden calves to be their gods in Bethel and Dan.

questions.question: What was the sin associated with Jeroboam's establishment of worship at Dan?
options: Worshipping idols instead of the LORD
Building an altar without the priests
Worshiping the LORD at the temple
questions.correctAnswer: Worshipping idols instead of the LORD
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:30 states that this became a sin because the people worshipped before the golden calf at Dan, which was idolatry.

questions.question: What was unusual about the priests Jeroboam appointed for his high places?
options: They were from the tribe of Levi
They were the lowest of the people, not Levites
They were prophets sent by God
questions.correctAnswer: They were the lowest of the people, not Levites
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:31 explains that Jeroboam made priests from the lowest of the people who were not from the sons of Levi, which was contrary to the Mosaic law.

questions.question: On what day and month did Jeroboam ordain a feast like that of Judah?
options: Fifteenth day of the eighth month
Tenth day of the seventh month
First day of the first month
Twentieth day of the ninth month
questions.correctAnswer: Fifteenth day of the eighth month
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:32 specifies that Jeroboam ordained the feast on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, mirroring Judah's feast.

questions.question: What was Jeroboam's reason for fearing that the kingdom might return to the house of David?
options: Because the people were dissatisfied with him
Because the people would go to Jerusalem to sacrifice and turn their hearts back
Because Rehoboam had a stronger army
Because of a prophecy from Ahijah
questions.correctAnswer: Because the people would go to Jerusalem to sacrifice and turn their hearts back
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:26-27 shows Jeroboam’s concern that if people went to worship in Jerusalem, their loyalty would shift back to Rehoboam.

questions.question: Which tribe remained loyal to the house of David after Israel rebelled?
questions.correctAnswer: Judah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:20 states that only the tribe of Judah followed the house of David after the kingdom split.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Jeroboam’s speech about his yoke compared to his father’s?
questions.correctAnswer: Hyperbole
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:10-11 uses exaggerated language (hyperbole) when Jeroboam says his little finger will be thicker than his father's loins and he will chastise with scorpions, to emphasize harsh rule.

questions.question: Which Old Testament prophet’s word was fulfilled by the division of the kingdom in this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Ahijah the Shilonite
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:15 indicates that the division happened according to the LORD's word spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of rebellion and division seen in 1 Kings 12?
questions.correctAnswer: Romans 11:17-24
questions.explanation: Romans 11:17-24 discusses the grafting in and out of branches, symbolizing division and rebellion among God's people, echoing the division in 1 Kings 12.

questions.question: What was the role of Adoram sent by Rehoboam to Israel, and what happened to him?
options: Overseer of tribute; he was stoned to death
Commander of the army; he was victorious
questions.correctAnswer: Overseer of tribute; he was stoned to death
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:18 recounts that Adoram, who was over tribute, was stoned by Israel, causing Rehoboam to flee to Jerusalem.

questions.question: True or False: Jeroboam consulted the Levites to serve as priests in his newly built high places.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:31 states Jeroboam made priests from the lowest people, not from the sons of Levi, violating priestly law.

questions.question: True or False: The division of the kingdom was part of God's plan to fulfill a prophecy given to Jeroboam.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:15 explicitly says the cause of the division was from the LORD to fulfill His word through Ahijah the Shilonite.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the word translated as 'high places' in the context of Jeroboam's worship sites?
options: Bamah, meaning elevated places for worship
questions.correctAnswer: Bamah, meaning elevated places for worship
questions.explanation: The term 'high places' is typically translated from the Hebrew 'Bamah,' referring to elevated sites used for worship, often associated with idolatry as in 1 Kings 12:31.

theological.title: 1 Kings Chapter 12 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Kings Chapter 12 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What divine purpose is revealed in Rehoboam's refusal to lighten the yoke upon Israel, as indicated in 1 Kings 12:14-15?
options: God allowed it to fulfill his prophecy spoken through Ahijah.
God was displeased and immediately punished Rehoboam.
God intended to restore Israel quickly after their rebellion.
God was unaware of the king's decision and its consequences.
questions.correctAnswer: God allowed it to fulfill his prophecy spoken through Ahijah.
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 12:14-15 states that Rehoboam's harsh response to Israel was from the LORD to perform what He had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite to Jeroboam. This shows divine sovereignty in allowing human decisions to fulfill divine prophecy.

questions.question: Which doctrine is taught by the people's rejection of Rehoboam with the words, 'What portion have we in David?' in 1 Kings 12:16?
options: Doctrine of the covenant and its conditionality.
Doctrine of predestination without human response.
questions.correctAnswer: Doctrine of the covenant and its conditionality.
questions.explanation: The people's rejection reflects the conditional nature of God's covenant with David's house, contingent on faithfulness and obedience, as implied in 1 Kings 12:16. This aligns with covenant theology principles.

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 12:22-24 reveal an attribute of God through the prophet Shemaiah's message to Rehoboam?
options: God demonstrates his sovereignty by restraining conflict among His people.
God shows indifference toward civil strife.
God condones war to punish disobedience.
God is unaware of the political division.
questions.correctAnswer: God demonstrates his sovereignty by restraining conflict among His people.
questions.explanation: Verses 22-24 show God’s sovereign control over Israel’s history, commanding peace and preventing civil war, demonstrating his providential governance (cf. Psalm 103:19).

questions.question: What theological implication arises from Jeroboam’s establishment of golden calves and unauthorized priesthood in 1 Kings 12:28-31?
options: It reveals the sinfulness of idolatry and rejection of proper worship.
It demonstrates God’s acceptance of multiple worship forms.
It shows the legitimacy of local shrines.
It indicates a new covenant practice.
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals the sinfulness of idolatry and rejection of proper worship.
questions.explanation: Jeroboam’s actions signify covenant unfaithfulness and idolatry, violating God's command for centralized worship, as explained in 1 Kings 12:28-31 and echoed in Deuteronomy 12:5-14.

questions.question: Based on 1 Kings 12:6-7 and 1 Kings 12:10-11, what combined teaching about human wisdom and divine counsel can be drawn from Rehoboam’s consultation with old and young advisors?
options: Human wisdom is fallible and divine counsel should be preferred.
Youthful counsel is superior to aged wisdom.
Human advice is irrelevant in divine matters.
Only military counsel matters in kingship.
questions.correctAnswer: Human wisdom is fallible and divine counsel should be preferred.
questions.explanation: The old men advised kindness leading to stable rule, but Rehoboam chose harsh counsel from young men (1 Kings 12:6-11). This reflects the theological principle that human wisdom can err and divine guidance is paramount (cf. Proverbs 3:5-6).

questions.question: How does the rebellion of Israel in 1 Kings 12:19 illustrate the doctrine of human depravity and the consequences of sin?
options: It shows humanity's tendency toward self-will and rejection of God's anointed.
It proves that people are inherently good and just.
It demonstrates that sin has no real consequences.
It teaches that rebellion is always justified.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows humanity's tendency toward self-will and rejection of God's anointed.
questions.explanation: Israel’s rebellion against David’s house exemplifies fallen humanity’s sinful nature and rejection of God-ordained authority, consistent with the doctrine of total depravity (1 Kings 12:19; Romans 3:10-12).

questions.question: What broader redemptive narrative is reflected by the division of the kingdom and Jeroboam’s reign over Israel apart from Judah, as described in 1 Kings 12:20-21?
options: The fracturing of God’s chosen people anticipating the Messiah’s unification mission.
The permanent separation of God’s people with no hope of restoration.
The fulfillment of Israel’s idolatrous destiny.
The end of God’s covenant promises.
questions.correctAnswer: The fracturing of God’s chosen people anticipating the Messiah’s unification mission.
questions.explanation: The kingdom’s division foreshadows the Messianic hope for future reconciliation and unity of God’s people, as the Messiah is to restore and gather Israel (cf. Ezekiel 37:15-28).

questions.question: What does Rehoboam’s quick flight to Jerusalem after the death of Adoram in 1 Kings 12:18 indicate about the political and spiritual consequences of rejecting God’s guidance?
options: Rehoboam’s instability and the unraveling of divine order due to disobedience.
His great wisdom and political savvy.
questions.correctAnswer: Rehoboam’s instability and the unraveling of divine order due to disobedience.
questions.explanation: The violent death of Adoram and Rehoboam’s flight reveal the chaos and judgment that result from rejecting God’s counsel, showing consequences of disobedience (1 Kings 12:18; cf. Proverbs 29:2).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s word in 1 Kings 12:24 commanding Rehoboam not to fight Israel shows divine favoritism and injustice. What does 1 Kings 12:22-24 actually teach about God’s justice and providence?
options: God’s command prevents fratricidal warfare and serves His providential plan for His people’s welfare.
God arbitrarily favors Judah over Israel.
God desires endless conflict among His people.
God is indifferent to human suffering.
questions.correctAnswer: God’s command prevents fratricidal warfare and serves His providential plan for His people’s welfare.
questions.explanation: The passage reveals God’s justice in restraining violence and His providence in guiding Israel’s history (1 Kings 12:22-24; cf. Romans 8:28). This counters claims of divine injustice.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted by the fulfillment of Ahijah the Shilonite’s prophecy through the events in 1 Kings 12:15 and the kingdom’s division?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness to His promises.
questions.explanation: The fulfillment of prophecy in the kingdom’s division demonstrates God’s unwavering faithfulness to His spoken word (1 Kings 12:15; cf. Isaiah 55:11).

questions.question: What does Jeroboam’s fear in 1 Kings 12:26-27 teach about the human response to divine judgment and the nature of sin?
options: Sin leads to fear of losing God’s favor and motivates further rebellion.
Sin is irrelevant to human kingship.
questions.correctAnswer: Sin leads to fear of losing God’s favor and motivates further rebellion.
questions.explanation: Jeroboam’s fear of losing his kingdom if people returned to Jerusalem shows how sin causes spiritual and political insecurity, often causing individuals to double down in disobedience (1 Kings 12:26-27).

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 12:31 reveal a theological problem caused by Jeroboam’s appointment of priests from among the lowest people?
options: A rejection of the Levitical priesthood and God’s ordained order.
A legitimate reform of priestly roles.
questions.correctAnswer: A rejection of the Levitical priesthood and God’s ordained order.
questions.explanation: Jeroboam’s choice of unqualified priests violates God’s command that priests come from Levi, highlighting a theological problem of illegitimate worship (1 Kings 12:31; cf. Leviticus 21:16-24).

questions.question: Which combined doctrinal insight emerges from 1 Kings 12:4 and 1 Kings 12:14 concerning kingship and the nature of authority?
options: Godly leadership requires humility and service, not harsh dominion.
Kingship is primarily about oppression and control.
Authority is justified only by force.
questions.correctAnswer: Godly leadership requires humility and service, not harsh dominion.
questions.explanation: The people’s request in verse 4 for lighter yoke contrasts with Rehoboam’s harsh response in verse 14, teaching that God’s ideal kingship is servant leadership (cf. Mark 10:42-45).

questions.question: What theological lesson about human pride and divine judgment can be synthesized from Rehoboam’s boast in 1 Kings 12:10-11 and the resulting rebellion in verses 16-19?
options: Prideful leadership leads to division and judgment by God.
Pride secures lasting peace and unity.
Divine judgment is unrelated to human actions.
questions.correctAnswer: Prideful leadership leads to division and judgment by God.
questions.explanation: Rehoboam’s arrogant words (12:10-11) provoke Israel’s rejection (12:16-19), illustrating the biblical principle that pride incurs divine judgment (cf. Proverbs 16:18).

questions.question: How does 1 Kings 12:25-33 contribute to understanding the persistent problem of syncretism and its impact on Israel’s covenant relationship with God?
options: It shows that syncretistic worship leads to sin and separation from God’s covenant.
It indicates God’s approval of blended worship practices.
It reveals that syncretism leads to greater unity.
It encourages innovation in religious observance.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that syncretistic worship leads to sin and separation from God’s covenant.
questions.explanation: Jeroboam’s establishment of unauthorized feasts and calves (12:25-33) illustrates syncretism causing covenant unfaithfulness and sin, which damages Israel’s relationship with God (cf. Hosea 4:12-13).
